title: skilldrop organisation policy
$comment: RFC-0050. The file an organisation hands out (--policy, SKILLDROP_POLICY, or ~/.config/skilldrop/policy.json). Closed at every level: an unknown key stops the command, because a misspelt rule that is silently ignored is a rule that isn't there. bin/governance.js enforces the same shape; contracts/policy.example.json must satisfy both.

note.description: Free text: who owns this policy and where to ask about it.

allow.description: Catalogue sources allowed: "bundled", a git URL (a trailing * matches a prefix, e.g. https://git.example.org/skills/*), or a path. Absent: any.

require_pinned.description: Every catalogue other than the bundled one must be pinned to a commit (--from <url>#<commit>).

allow.description: Skill, loop and agent names allowed; * matches anything. Absent: any.

max.description: The worst supply-chain scan finding a skill may carry: none, low (🟨), medium (🟧), high (🟥). Findings in eval fixtures and example inputs never count.

audit.description: Present: install, update and uninstall append to a tamper-evident log.

log.description: Where the log goes. Default ~/.config/skilldrop/audit.jsonl. Refused inside a git working tree.

actor.description: Who each entry names: "pseudonym" (default; a keyed hash of user and machine, needs the salt), "none", "os-user", or {"fixed": "<name>"} such as a team or machine id.

salt_env.description: The environment variable holding the organisation's secret salt for pseudonyms. Default SKILLDROP_AUDIT_SALT.
